title: Pricing by hours per project for Aquarium maintenance
audience: Owners and supervisors of aquarium maintenance businesses, freshwater and marine, who write quotes for visits, tank cleans and rehoming jobs, and need a price that covers cost and earns a margin.
learningOutcomes: Calculate a cost per productive hour from the owner's own figures
Estimate visit and project hours, including set-up, travel, fish-holding time and checking time
Build a quote from hours, a rate and a margin, and state its basis and exclusions

instruction.heading: Why hours are the starting unit
instruction.body: An aquarium visit is a short job at the site with a drive either side of it. The crew's time, the travel, the set-up and the readings all become hours. Once you know the hours, you can see the cost, the margin and the effect of a change in scope, such as adding a marine test or a full tank clean. A flat price with no hours behind it hides both risk and waste, and it is hard to defend when a client asks why a visit costs what it does.

instruction.heading: Build the cost per productive hour
instruction.body: Take the total cost of running the business over a period and divide it by the productive hours in the same period. Total cost includes wages with on-costs such as leave and superannuation, where your staff arrangements require them, vehicle running costs, test kits and consumables not charged separately, equipment, insurance, administration and premises. Productive hours are the hours spent on chargeable work at the tank, not the paid hours on a roster. Use billable hours as the divisor. For illustration only, if you pay for 40 hours and 30 of them are chargeable, the cost per productive hour is higher than the hourly wage. Business.gov.au says on-costs such as super and leave belong in the hourly figure (1 October 2026).

instruction.heading: Estimate the hours
instruction.body: Break each visit into tasks: the readings, the water change, the glass and substrate, the filter service, the equipment check and the visit note. Estimate each task at a standard speed, then add set-up, pack-down, travel and a checking allowance. Where fish must be held in a tub while a tank is drained or moved, price that holding time as a named line, not as a hidden extra. Add a set allowance for delays outside your control, such as access problems or staff absence. Xero Australia suggests adding 10 to 20 percent to job estimates for unexpected work (3 September 2026); use that as a starting point and size your own allowance from your records. Record the actual hours after each job and note the reason for any gap.

instruction.heading: Turn hours into a price
instruction.body: Multiply the crew hours by the cost per productive hour to get the cost of the visit or project. Add a margin that reflects your target and the risk, such as a neglected tank, a large tank, or a tight deadline for a move. Apply your materials policy and your minimum charge. Where tank water must be discarded, the research found a Queensland fact sheet that says tank water may carry eggs or larvae and should not be siphoned into drains. It does not say the same for New South Wales, where the rule was not confirmed. The Unitywater and Icon Water discharge rules in this course cover pool water, and they must not be applied to aquarium water.

instruction.heading: Keep the quote honest
instruction.body: A quote should state the scope, the hours or price basis, the exclusions, what the client must provide, and how long the quote is valid. Exclusions for an aquarium quote usually include fish rehoming and release, fish-health treatment, marine livestock, and water disposal beyond the agreed method. Do not show the internal cost per hour to the client unless your policy says to. The ACCC says misleading price statements are prohibited (setting prices: what's allowed, 15 July 2026). Re-quote whenever the scope changes.

instruction.heading: Review your estimates
instruction.body: Compare estimated and actual hours for at least the first ten visits or projects of each type. Carters Trade Leader recommends using the gap between quoted and actual labour to correct the next quote (1 October 2025). If the variance stays above a threshold you have agreed, change the standard time, the margin or the scope rules. The research found no aquarium cost-per-hour benchmark, so your own records are the only source for this figure.

procedure: Gather the year's total business costs and the productive hours achieved in the same period.
Divide total costs by productive hours to get the cost per productive hour.
Break the visit into tasks, including the readings, the water change and the filter service, and estimate each task time as a range.
Add set-up, pack-down, travel and checking time as named lines, and add any fish-holding time as its own line.
Multiply total crew hours by the cost per productive hour, then apply the margin for risk and target.
Apply the materials policy and the minimum charge, and price any water disposal only after checking the local rule.
Write the quote with scope, hours basis, exclusions, client inputs and validity.
Record actual hours after each job and compare them with the estimate.

workedExamples.situation: Illustrative figures only, not market rates. A freshwater tank visit takes 2.0 crew-hours on site and 0.5 crew-hours of travel. The owner's cost per productive hour is $60 AUD (illustrative). The target margin on price is 25 per cent (illustrative). No aquarium visit rate with a stated unit was found to check the result against.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What is the cost of the visit and its price, and what changes if a marine tank also needs a 1-hour fish-holding period during a rehoming?
workedExamples.reasoning: The cost is 2.5 crew-hours multiplied by $60 AUD, which is $150 AUD (illustrative). A 25 per cent margin on price means the price is the cost divided by 0.75, which gives $200 AUD (illustrative). A 1-hour fish-holding period adds 1.0 crew-hour, so the cost becomes $210 AUD and the price becomes $280 AUD (illustrative). The holding time is a named line, agreed in writing before the visit, and the owner confirms that the fish will go to a named new home or retailer rather than being released.

equipmentAndPpe: Time log for each visit or project, with estimated and actual columns
Holding tub and aeration kit, where fish must be held on site

commonErrors.error: Pricing from the hourly wage alone
commonErrors.prevention: Include on-costs, vehicle, equipment, insurance and administration in the cost per productive hour.

commonErrors.error: Counting paid hours as productive hours
commonErrors.prevention: Use chargeable hours only when calculating the cost per productive hour.

commonErrors.error: Leaving out travel, set-up, fish-holding and checking time
commonErrors.prevention: Add these as named lines on every estimate.

commonErrors.error: Applying pool discharge rules to an aquarium
commonErrors.prevention: Check a rule written for aquarium water first; the pool rules in this course do not apply to tanks.

commonErrors.error: Never comparing estimates with actual hours
commonErrors.prevention: Record actual hours after each visit and review the variance monthly.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: This is pricing guidance only. The Australian Consumer Law applies to pricing statements, and the ACCC says misleading statements about prices are prohibited. State or territory fair trading rules also apply and differ between states, so check the rules for your state.

Fish rules affect what you can price. Releasing fish into New South Wales public waters is illegal without a permit, and Queensland says fish must never be released. Do not price fish release or relocation until the state rule has been checked.

Pay rates, allowances and on-costs for employees may be set by an award or enterprise agreement. Award coverage for aquarium workers was not checked in this course. Confirm which instrument applies to each worker before using any cost figure.

qualityStandard: Each quote shows scope, hours or price basis, exclusions, client inputs and validity.
The cost per productive hour is calculated from the owner's own records and dated.
Actual hours are recorded for at least the first ten visits or projects of each type and compared with the estimate.
No quote is issued without a margin decision and a minimum-charge check.
documentationEvidence: Cost per productive hour worksheet, dated, with the source of each figure
Quote showing scope, hours basis, exclusions and validity
Visit time log with estimated and actual hours
summary: Hours make the work visible, so start every quote from hours.
Cost per productive hour uses chargeable time, not paid time.
Travel, set-up, fish-holding and checking time are named lines, not hidden extras.
Compare estimates with actual hours, and change the method when they diverge.

knowledgeChecks.question: Which costs belong in the cost per productive hour for an aquarium business?
options: Only the hourly wage of the lowest-paid worker and nothing else from the accounts or the rent
The price the client pays, plus the deposit, the late fee and the crew bonus paid
The average hourly rate of other aquarium businesses in the local area and their fees for the whole year
Wages with on-costs, vehicle, equipment, consumables, insurance and administration, divided by chargeable hours

knowledgeChecks.question: A tank visit is estimated at 2.5 crew-hours and takes 4. What is the right response?
options: Record the actual hours, find the cause, and adjust the estimate and future quotes
Leave the estimate, since the client has already paid and the crew has finished
Reduce paid hours for the crew on the next job and skip the morning break
Raise the price for this client's next visit only and no one else is charged more

knowledgeChecks.question: Why does an aquarium quote need an exclusions list?
options: To hide the margin from the client and to keep the rates a secret from the crew
To make the quote longer and to fill up the page with more text and words for the client
To show what the price covers, so scope changes can be priced and disputes are reduced
To lower the client's expectations and to make the job seem much smaller than it is

sourceReferences: business.gov.au, 'Choose a pricing strategy', https://business.gov.au/products-and-services/choose-a-pricing-strategy, page metadata dated 1 October 2026. Supports: on-costs such as super and leave belong in the hourly cost; a quote should recover cost and add a margin.
ACCC, 'Setting prices: what's allowed', https://www.accc.gov.au/business/pricing/setting-prices-whats-allowed, last modified 15 July 2026. Supports: misleading price statements are prohibited.

Xero Australia, 'How to price services', https://www.xero.com/au/guides/how-to-price-services/, dated 3 September 2026. Supports: divide by billable hours, not total hours; add 10 to 20 percent to job estimates for unexpected work.

Carters Trade Leader, 'Estimating how many hours a job will take', https://tradeleader.carters.co.nz/trade-skills/estimating-how-many-hours-a-job-will-take-why-83-get-it-wrong/, dated 1 October 2025. New Zealand publisher; general method only. Supports: use the gap between quoted and actual labour to correct the next quote.

Queensland Department of Agriculture and Fisheries, 'Ipa aquarium fish importation' fact sheet, https://www.daf.qld.gov.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0004/1457824/ipa-aquarium-fish-importation.pdf, dated June 2020. Supports: tank water may carry eggs or larvae and should not be siphoned into drains; fish must not be released.

NSW DPI, 'Freshwater pest fish in NSW', Primefact 1336, https://www.dpi.nsw.gov.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0010/637129/Primefact-1336-Freshwater-pest-fish-in-NSW.pdf, September 2023. Supports: releasing fish into NSW public waters without a permit is illegal.

Gap: no aquarium cost-per-hour, labour rate or aquarium discharge rule for New South Wales or any other state was found. Award and enterprise agreement coverage for aquarium workers was not checked. No trade-body or fish-keeping club source was reached.
